headline: Bank of Jamaica raises policy rate to 6.50% to contain inflation
summary: The Bank of Jamaica's Monetary Policy Committee unanimously decided to increase the policy rate by 50 basis points to 6.50% to address inflationary pressures.
why: Central bank rate decisions are the primary tool for managing inflation and stabilizing the national economy.

impacts.name: Jamaica Policy Rate
impacts.why: The central bank raised rates to combat inflation.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Higher interest rates increase the cost of borrowing, which is intended to slow down spending and reduce inflationary pressure in the economy.
